summary:
We developed HANOI Earth Lab, a comprehensive "3-in-1" educational ecosystem consisting of a web-based data analyzer, an interactive comic, and a physical testing diorama. Our project addresses the challenge by simplifying complex climate trends—specifically precipitation, land surface temperature, and vegetation changes. Instead of passively reading charts, students engage through a multi-sensory journey: they follow an immersive narrative with "Tí Tách the Raindrop," analyze real NASA satellite data (utilizing AppEEARS and GPM IMERG), and conduct hands-on experiments to verify their predictions.

This project is important because it bridges the gap between abstract textbook definitions and real-world environmental dynamics. By transforming dry Earth science statistics into an age-appropriate adventure, we foster systems thinking and proactive research habits in primary and middle school students. Ultimately, HANOI Earth Lab awakens compassion for nature and equips students with the digital literacy needed to become responsible global citizens who actively protect our planet.
details:
HANOI Earth Lab (Team: Galaxy DTD_2026) is a comprehensive "3-in-1" educational ecosystem designed to help students decode complex climate change trends from 2005 to 2025. The project operates seamlessly across three interconnected platforms: a Web Lab that visualizes NASA's satellite data archives (allowing students to track precipitation, temperature, and vegetation via a timeline slider), an immersive interactive comic following "Tí Tách the Raindrop" through data-decoding challenges, and a hands-on physical diorama for conducting real-world runoff experiments.

Our breakthrough creativity lies in a multi-sensory approach that perfectly intersects digital storytelling with data analytics. Instead of passively reading charts, students engage comprehensively by exploring the narrative, analyzing real data, and physically testing their predictions. To bring this vision to life, we utilized core NASA data—including AppEEARS, Worldview, GPM IMERG, LST, and NDVI. The digital platforms were developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript alongside digital illustration tools, while the physical model was constructed from craft materials and mini water pump systems.

During development, we carefully considered age-appropriate scaffolding to maximize educational impact. The experience is tailored to captivate primary school students through animated characters and tangible models, while simultaneously stimulating middle school students with critical satellite chart analysis. Furthermore, to ensure global scalability, the project intentionally minimizes text. By utilizing colors and visual imagery as a universal language, we have built a foundation for seamless multi-language localization in the future.

Ultimately, HANOI Earth Lab simplifies dry Earth science statistics into an engaging adventure, bridging the gap between abstract textbook definitions and real-world environmental dynamics. By fostering systems thinking and proactive research habits, the project aspires to awaken a deep compassion for nature. We aim to equip students with essential digital skills, empowering them to become confident global citizens who take proactive responsibility for protecting our planet.
